chunks: If We had pleased to make a plaything We could have made it Ourself, if We had cared to do so.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God creating a plaything or deity from Himself?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a refutation of the Qarmatian and Ismaili claim that God might have a 'son' or an emanated deity, affirming His absolute transcendence (Tanzih) from any physical or spiritual offspring. It underscores that divine creation is an act of will rather than necessity, distinguishing the Creator from the created to preserve monotheistic purity against anthropomorphic or polytheistic attributions.
